facts.statement: Dolichochampsa was an extinct genus of eusuchian crocodylomorph.
facts.quote: Dolichochampsa is an extinct genus of eusuchian crocodylomorph.

facts.statement: Dolichochampsa is the sole member of the family Dolichochampsidae.
facts.quote: It is the type genus and only member of the family Dolichochampsidae.

facts.statement: Dolichochampsa possessed a distinctive slender snout.
facts.quote: It had a distinctive slender snout.

facts.statement: Fossils of Dolichochampsa have been found in the Yacoraite Formation of Argentina and the El Molino Formation of Bolivia.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in the Yacoraite Formation of Argentina and the El Molino Formation of Bolivia of Maastrichtian age.

facts.statement: The relationships of Dolichochampsa with other eusuchians remain unknown due to fragmentary fossil material.
facts.quote: Because the material associated with the specimens is so fragmentary, its relationships with other eusuchians remain unknown.

facts.statement: Dolichochampsa lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Dolichochampsa is Dolichochampsa minima.
Dolichochampsa belongs to the parent group Gavialoidea.
